subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what exact trigger plus local editor/tempfile safety contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation shape is clear, but launching $VISUAL/$EDITOR and writing prompt drafts to disk is a product and security boundary that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Approve guarded core TUI flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Keep open pending UX choice
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers choose the shortcut or slash-command model and decide whether to reuse or replace the inactive external-editor keybinding entry.

options.title: Decline external process handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing and composer expansion rather than launching local editors from the TUI.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded core TUI flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact request and has recent history on the same TUI command and shortcut surfaces.
